clauses.quote: We do not permit the Use of any third-party software, tools, or programs that interact with the Services that give one player an unintended, unnatural, or unfair advantage over another player. Such prohibited third-party software, tools, or programs include those that alter Game-balance in favor of one player over another, automate actions within the Services, promote unattended gameplay, or have an adverse effect on other users of the Services. Prohibited third-party programs will be determined at our sole discretion.
clauses.source: Guild Wars 2 User Agreement, Section 2.1.3 (Prohibited Third-Party Programs)
clauses.title: Third-party programs

clauses.quote: Use, obtain, or provide data related to the operation of the Services, including, but not limited to, software that reads areas of computer memory or storage devices; intercepts or otherwise collects data; or redirects, creates, maintains, or emulates the Services.
clauses.source: Guild Wars 2 User Agreement, Section 3.1 (Rules of Conduct)
clauses.title: Modifying or reading the client

clauses.quote: Create, use, offer, promote, or distribute any cheats, bots, or hacks.
clauses.source: Guild Wars 2 User Agreement, Section 3.1 (Rules of Conduct)
clauses.title: Automation and bots

clauses.quote: You use any third-party program at your own risk.
clauses.source: Guild Wars 2 Support: Policy: Third-Party Programs
clauses.title: Third-party programs are used at your own risk

clauses.quote: With that said, we are aware that some utilities help players without affecting others; that is, they do not give one player an advantage over another. While, in general, we will not take action on an account for the use of such a utility program or modification, action is subject to ArenaNet's discretion. You use any third-party program at your own risk.
clauses.source: Guild Wars 2 Support: Policy: Third-Party Programs
clauses.title: Utilities that do not affect other players

clauses.quote: The best way for you to assess whether a specific third-party program could have any impact on another player is to ask: "Does this program allow someone to play faster, better, longer, or more accurately than someone who doesn't use the program?" "Does this program allow someone to 'play' when he/she is not at the computer?" "Does this program allow the user to gain unnatural or undeserved rewards?"
clauses.source: Guild Wars 2 Support: Policy: Third-Party Programs
clauses.title: The test ArenaNet asks players to apply

clauses.quote: Attended macro use is permitted as long as it is not exploitative, and as long as it does not provide the user with an unfair advantage over other players. Unattended macro use is prohibited under any circumstances.
clauses.source: Guild Wars 2 Support: Policy: Macros and Macro Use
clauses.title: Macros: attended use permitted, unattended prohibited

clauses.quote: Here are few common macros that are allowed in the game: You may bind dodge and jump to a single key. You may create an auto-clicker that opens or consumes a stack of items. You may use music macros to compose or perform in-game music. As long as the macro is used solely for the composition or performance of in-game music and the account is actively attended by a player, we do not place restrictions on its use.
clauses.source: Guild Wars 2 Support: Policy: Macros and Macro Use
clauses.title: Macros ArenaNet explicitly allows

clauses.quote: However, here are some of the scenarios that are not permitted in the game: Macro use cannot interfere with the gameplay of other players. You cannot program a macro to perform actions on more than one account at a time. You cannot use macros to automate skill use while away from your computer. You cannot use macros to create skill chains in any competitive environment, including PvP, WvW, open world activities, races, etc. You cannot use macros to participate in activities or events, such as Bell Choir. You cannot use macros for the sole purpose of farming items, currencies, karma, or other benefits in the game, particularly while away from the keyboard (AFK). You cannot use macros to fully automate a character (“bot”) in the game. Each macro should represent a single action that requires user input before repeating the action.
clauses.source: Guild Wars 2 Support: Policy: Macros and Macro Use
clauses.title: Macro uses that are not permitted

clauses.quote: Any use of the APIs must comply with ArenaNet's Content Terms of Use and Website Terms of Use. Use of the APIs constitutes acceptance of the terms and conditions contained in the ArenaNet Content Terms of Use, Website Terms of Use, and any related terms or conditions when they are posted.
clauses.source: Guild Wars 2 Wiki: API:Main (Guild Wars 2 API Terms of Use)
clauses.title: API terms of use
